evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep skipped straight into move details without time-boxing or waiting for confirmation. Opened with 'I have your personalized estimate ready' and jumped directly to confirming existing details.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep began with logistics confirmation and moved immediately into problem-solving (unmounting screens, packing).
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer raised no unprompted concerns; all responses were reactions to rep's specific questions about the move logistics.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns raised by customer that would require reflection.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Covered: property type (office), floors, elevator access, unmounting needs, packing approach, timeline (Friday packing, Saturday move). Missing: room count, walking distance from truck, additional stops.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Yes — 'Do you need our help to pack those items into boxes or will you be able to do it yourself?'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: No box count or overflow check offered.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full — gave typical range ($2,472–$2,884) for four movers and two trucks, six to seven hours, personalized to office setup, unmounting work, and stated confidence customer might finish faster.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full — disclosed hourly rate ($412/hr for four movers and two trucks), stated all inclusions (fuel, insurance, pads, tools, assembly), explicitly listed no hidden fees (no transportation, disassembly, storage, credit card fees), and mentioned 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked — rep moved directly from pricing explanation into perks without gauging customer reaction to the estimate itself.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full — 'if we cannot make it in the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill' with clear clock mechanics.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full — '$2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for any accidental damages' with no mention of deductible or fine print.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No — rep did not ask 'does that put those to rest?' or confirm the two promises settled the customer's concerns before moving on.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway — 'do you have any questions or anything for me' is generic ask-any-questions language, not genuine 'what's still concerning you.'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No — never asked 'anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or similar catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never — rep asked 'would you like me to get you on the schedule or send you an email for now?' which gives customer an out (email) without asking for the business directly. Customer accepted the out ('send me an email for now') and rep accepted without re-asking.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Yes — 'to secure a spot, there's no deposit required.'

top_strength: Nicole delivered a thorough, transparent pricing explanation with all key disclosures (hourly rate, inclusions, no hidden fees, minimum, increments) and both promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) fully articulated and easy to understand.
coaching_note: This was a routed walkthrough call (office move with custom logistics) that Nicole should have recognized and scheduled cleanly instead of pricing on the phone — but because she did quote, she skipped critical steps: no quid pro quo framing at the open, no genuine concerns check at the end, and no explicit ask for the business (gave customer an easy out with email instead of asking plainly for the booking).
booking_note: Customer explicitly requested email instead of booking: 'If you could send me an email for now because I do have another quote that I'm waiting for... an email would be perfect'
